items.title: APEC深圳峰會：習近平親赴機場迎接特朗普，46年來首次中國元首接機

items.title: 美中俄峰會：為何選在深圳麒麟山莊？習仲勳、金正日都曾下榻

items.title: 黃仁勳婚外情掀「中國間諜」迷因：幽默與偏見之間，亞裔女性如何自處？

items.title: 特朗普訪華之際 美國封堵中國公司在東南亞租用AI算力的「後門」
items.desc: 在美國限制最先進英偉達芯片直接銷往中國的背景下，中國大型互聯網公司和AI實驗室逐漸轉向「只租算力、不買硬件」的模式。芯片部署在第三國數據中心，中國企業再通過互聯網遠程調用算力訓練模型，而無須把相關硬件運入中國。

items.title: 高雄選戰「知識藍」對決「新潮流」，國民黨能複製「韓流」嗎？
items.desc: 柯志恩以「知識藍」的姿態拉攏中間選民，支持度大幅追貼深耕高雄20年的賴瑞隆，選情咬緊。

items.title: 「藍白合」示範區：新竹市選情如何透露台灣第三勢力的未來？
items.desc: 新竹市是民眾黨此前唯一贏得執政權的縣市，現任市長高虹安尋求連任，她這次雖已退出民眾黨、改以無黨籍身分參選，但學者指出其選情不僅將影響雙方未來合作模式能否延續，也可能牽動2028年全國大選的政治布局。

items.title: 九合一前夕：台灣幾乎年年選舉，會引起「投票疲勞」嗎？
items.desc: 台灣在過去七年間，幾乎每年都有大型選舉、罷免或公投。有學者形容台灣政治人物常處於「選舉模式」，在面對不同議題時往往急於回應。

items.title: 里長赴中旅遊受關注：為何北京鎖定里長？里長怎麼看？
items.desc: 台灣地方選舉即將到來，近年北京對台統戰工作重心從政商菁英轉向基層社會，而里長作為選舉期間的地方「樁腳」，就成為了北京的重要接觸對象。

items.title: 「九合一」五大看點：「洋流」能否撼動台北？誰在卡位2028？
items.desc: 中共是否介入台灣選舉？ 這次選舉將如何影響賴清德與國民黨主席鄭麗文的政治能量？捲土重來、希望藉著地方議員選舉有所斬獲的小黨，此次結盟能否在主流政黨夾殺中突圍而出？

items.title: 美國今年已10人死於麻疹 26年後失去「麻疹消除狀態」
items.desc: 美國時隔26年失去麻疹消除狀態，今年病例達5400例、死亡10人，創1990年代以來新高。「疫苗懷疑論」持續遭到質疑。

items.title: APEC深圳峰會：賴清德派施振榮出席 台灣參會空間再成焦點

items.title: APEC深圳觀察：習近平想告訴世界，中國掌握著未來
items.desc: 當世界領導人本週齊聚深圳，他們將看到一座代表中國未來的科技之城：機器人、AI、摩天大樓，處處展現蓬勃的創新活力。但這很可能只是故事的一半：因為峰會停工的建築工人、為生計奔波的零工群體，對未來有著不同的想像。

items.title: 中國以AI奇境接待各國領袖，但他們看不到的另一面是什麼？
items.desc: 離開深圳充滿科技感的天際線後，你將會看到習近平治下中國所面臨的種種挑戰。

items.title: 歐盟峰會前夕 貝安德稱英國脫歐「得不償失」
items.desc: 英國首相在倫敦金融城市長晚宴上向與會人士表示，「我們得到的脫歐結果並沒有奏效」。

items.title: 俄羅斯超級富豪們已經在設想一個「後普京時代」
items.desc: 一些俄羅斯富豪渴望回到90年代的寡頭政治體制，當時商人掌握著權力。

items.title: 里長赴中旅遊：台灣《反滲透法》為何「查辦多、定罪少」？
items.desc: 台灣「九合一」地方選舉進入倒數，北京試圖介入台灣選舉的相關活動再受關注。台灣《反滲透法》施行後，儘管近年相關案件數量快速增加，但查辦近600人，只有5人被定罪，使現行法律規範與執法標準受到外界檢視。

items.title: 羅伯·派汀森：《暮光之城》男主角如何成為007
items.desc: 羅伯·派汀森（Robert Pattinson）早已在《暮光之城》系列、《蝙蝠俠》和《奧德賽》等電影，奠定了自己作為男主角、動作明星及演員的地位。如今，他接下詹姆士·龐德（James Bond；占士邦）一角，將使他的知名度更上一層樓。

items.title: 中國AI之都：「夢想之城」深圳背後的兩個世界
items.desc: 深圳被譽為中國最具未來感的城市之一。在本週的APEC峰會，中國國家主席習近平將在這裡接待包括美國總統特朗普和俄羅斯總統普京在內的多國領袖，向他們展示這座中國的人工智慧之都。但這座城市還有另一面，是領袖們看不到的。

items.title: 無法複製的奇蹟？深圳如何從改革開放樣板變為「中國矽谷」
items.desc: 深圳首次主辦亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）領導人峰會，成為中國的第三座主辦城市。深圳的崛起往往被視為中國改革開放最成功的一場實驗。而在中國和世界變幻莫測的今天，這個高速發展的奇蹟還能延續嗎？

items.title: 台灣村里長：最基層的民選公職，如何牽動選舉動員與兩岸關係？
items.desc: 村里長是台灣最基層的民選公職，因為掌握地方人脈，在社區服務與選舉動員中扮演重要角色。近年部分里長赴中國交流，引發北京透過基層網絡影響台灣政治的疑慮。BBC中文走訪台灣多個縣市，訪問三位不同世代、不同政治背景的里長，探討地方政治、兩岸交流與統戰之間的界線。

items.title: 「台灣之光」形象重挫？民眾如何看黃仁勳婚外情風波
items.desc: 輝達（英偉達）執行長黃仁勳捲入婚外情風波，部分美國媒體引述情報官員指，涉事女子與中國情報系統有關。BBC中文在台北街頭採訪民眾，了解他們如何看待這場仍在持續發醇的風波。

items.title: 美國中期選舉掀「藍色浪潮」 將怎樣影響世界

items.title: 「讓黃仁勳回歸」運動：輝達駁斥、特朗普支持恢復其CEO職位

items.title: 美國人如何背棄特朗普—

items.title: 黃仁勳曾告訴我，那些關於中國與國家安全的問題

items.title: 普京提議中美俄「三方會談」：特朗普響應，北京未表態，基輔反對

items.desc: Hung Cao says shipping insurance costs have soared to $64m for a single transit, challenging claims the strait is open.

items.desc: Many Palestinians started to flee refugee camps as the Israeli offensive got underway.

items.desc: Iran and the US have continued to exchange strikes in recent days, but all-out war has so far been avoided.

items.title: ‘Crimea is turning into an island’: How Ukraine hit Putin’s prized bridge
items.desc: A weeks-long operation was behind two waves of strikes using long-range missiles and drones developed in Ukraine.

items.title: Why Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea
items.desc: A Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Monday night brought down a stretch of the bridge linking the annexed Crimean Peninsula to Russia, potentially crippling a route long used by Moscow to move men and materiel into Crimea and the southern front. Here’s why Kyiv keeps testing its strength against an infrastructure project that has become synonymous with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s 2014 seizure of the peninsula.

items.title: Beijing has supported Moscow but 'China understands that America is way more important than Russia'
items.desc: Following Xi Jinping's very friendly rare tarmac greeting for Donald Trump, Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Kerry Brown, Professor of Chinese Studies and Director of the Lau China Institute at King's College, London. Brown examines the complex relationship between the world's two largest economies, China's growing diplomatic influence and the competition over artificial intelligence.“China is the diplomatic center of the world,” says Brown, pointing to Beijing's ability to bring together leaders from Russia, the United States, Europe and elsewhere. He argues that China now has “extraordinary convening power" and significant influence over Russia.

items.title: French ex-PM Philippe pledges to slash spending, hike retirement age as Elysée bid falters
items.desc: Former prime minister Édouard Philippe pledged on Wednesday to slash public spending, scrap France’s statutory 35-hour workweek and raise the retirement age to 65 from the current 62.9 years as he unveiled a slew of measures aimed a staving off economic "catastrophe" for France. An early frontrunner in next year's presidential election, Philippe is now trailing rivals in opinion polls and at risk of missing out on the second-round runoff.

items.title: War in Ukraine: Is France in direct conflict with Russia?
items.desc: An investigation published by the French public radio channel RFI on November 17 revealed that a confidential mission by the French army known as "Volia" has been used for months to conceal the presence of French personnel in Ukraine. Russia was prompt to accuse France of direct involvement in the conflict. Is this true?

items.title: Senate leadership challenge exposes divisions among Democrat
items.desc: As Democrats prepare to take control of the Senate, incumbent minority leader Chuck Schumer is facing an insurgent leadership bid from Senator Chris Van Hollen and disputes over party leadership are exposing divisions over what direction to take the Democratic party after their midterms sweep.

items.title: Russia’s new low-cost munitions pose a fresh threat to Ukraine
items.desc: Dan-T, Filin and Geran-5 might not mean anything to you, but in Ukraine, everyone is talking about these munitions. These new Russian weapons are small, fast and cheap – and a major threat, as they were specially designed to get around Ukrainian anti-aircraft defences and strike deep within the country.

items.title: Israel begins new military operation in Gaza
items.desc: Israeli tanks advanced in an area of the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its ​forces were targeting ‌Hamas infrastructure outside the "Yellow Line" that sets the boundary of the part of the enclave controlled by Israel  "The IDF launched a precise operation within the Gaza Strip earlier today west of the Yellow Line... to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip," the military said.

items.title: Gazans flee shelters as Israeli army launches ground operation beyond Yellow Line
items.desc: Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central Gaza on Wednesday after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it withdrew ​from under a ‌2025 ceasefire. The Israeli army said it crossed the Yellow Line separating Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas "to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip".

items.title: Yemen: Why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it
items.desc: Bolstered by their recent military successes, Houthi rebels this week advanced close to the southern port city of Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemeni government. Amid territorial ambitions, regional rivalries, and divisions within government forces, the potential fall of this stronghold could permanently alter the balance of power in the country.

items.title: 🔴 US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
items.desc: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to be the next speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on track to make history as the nation’s first Black American with the gavel.

items.title: French presidential elections 2027: More candidates, more confusion (Episode 2)
items.desc: France will head to the polls to vote for its next president in the spring of 2027. Thirty-eight candidates are currently vying to make it onto the final ballot and have until March 12 to gather backing from 500 elected officials. One figure currently stands out: Marine Le Pen. The far-right National Rally leader has a significant lead in the latest polls.

items.title: WHO sounds alarm over antibiotic resistance
items.desc: The World Health Organization sounded the alarm Monday over antimicrobial resistance, saying the world is off pace to meet key 2030 targets. Many countries have long neglected funding to track and detect dangerous microbes that resist antibiotic treatment, according to a report by the body.

items.title: Xi embraces Trump in China: 'Diplomacy playing out in real time'
items.desc: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Reporting from Shenzhen, France 24's Jan Camenzind Broomby says the warm greeting was a "big sign of respect" from Xi but also a calculated component of diplomatic efforts.

items.title: Xi welcomes Trump to China ahead of high
items.desc: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Beijing has indicated the war in Ukraine will not be discussed during the trilateral meeting, but Trump had said the conflict would find its way onto the agenda, something that experts say is likely to please Putin.

items.title: Three leaders, three agendas: Who wants what from Xi-Trump
items.desc: Be it curbing arms sales to Taiwan, bouncing back after a midterms shellacking, or the optics of a place at the table with the world's two superpowers, Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are approaching their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen with starkly different aims and agendas. Here's a look at what the Chinese, US and Russian leaders are hoping for.

items.title: US strikes Iranian island after Tehran targets Bahrain
items.desc: The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.

items.title: Why are measles cases soaring in the US?
items.desc: The United States has lost its long-held status of having eradicated measles as cases of the dangerous and highly contagious virus soar around the country. It follows accusations by medical experts that US President Donald Trump and his health secretary, noted vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, have fanned distrust in vaccinations, leading to an decline on the number of children getting inoculated against the disease.

items.title: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond: The surprise casting choice explained
items.desc: Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond, taking over from Daniel Craig in one of cinema’s most iconic roles. Film critic Emma Jones joins Eve Jackson on the arts24 weekly film show to discuss the surprise choice, Pattinson's star power and what he could bring to 007. Plus, they review the latest "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping", Lukas Dhont's Cannes prize winner "Coward" and Germany's Oscar entry "Everytime".

items.title: The calisson: A sweet taste of France's Provence region
items.desc: If you've ever visited the south of France, you may have come across a calisson. These traditional yellow and white almond-shaped candies are everywhere in the region. We tell you all about them with our guest Alexis Bertucat, head of communication and tourism for renowned calisson maker Confiserie du Roy René.

items.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race in historic victory
items.desc: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and becoming the first Democrat to win a US ‌Senate seat in the state in nearly 20 years and the first Alaska Native ever to do so.

items.title: 'A not so veiled criticism of the US' as Xi blasts protectionism at APEC summit
items.desc: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism and said regional economies needed to stand up to rising unilateralism in what France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani says was a "a not so veiled criticism of the US". Xi's comments came APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where a highly anticipated trilateral meeting between Xi, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin is set to take place on Thursday.

items.title: North Korea completes external works on enrichment facility extension, says IAEA
items.desc: A new extension to North Korea's Yongbyon enrichment facility has been "externally complete" since mid-October, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which relies on satellite imagery and open sources to monitor the country's nuclear programme. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi on Wednesday said expansion of Pyongyang's enrichment programme remains "cause for serious concern".

items.title: 'Extreme wealth can become a type of brain damage': Journalist Alexander Hurst
items.desc: An international journalist who poured his meagre savings into highly risky options trading at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic and quickly made $1.2 million, before losing it all again, has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his experience. Alexander Hurst works for a number of media outlets, including the Guardian as a correspondent based in Paris.
